To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) a platoon is vulnerable to a misbehavior attack that causes a platoon to stop; (2) the attack is effective against platoons with up to 100 vehicles; (3) a misbehaving vehicle can be detected by the vehicles in front of it; and (4) the attack can be prevented with a platoon size limit of 10 vehicles.

(a) a malicious car can cause significant harm to the rest of a platoon by simply accelerating, (b) a malicious car that can only accelerate or decelerate cannot cause harm to the rest if the rest of the platoon is cooperative, (c) a platoon that is not cooperative can still be made cooperative with a small amount of communication, and (d) a malicious car cannot cause significant harm if the rest of a non-cooperative platoon is cooperative.
